newsitem.title: ESTONIA: STOCKS MIXED AS BOURSE FAILS TO RECOVER.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS MIXED AS BOURSE FAILS TO RECOVER.

text.p: * Total trade was 70 million kroons on Thursday compared to
80 million kroons on Wednesday.
* Talse fell 0.79 percent to close on 266.70.
* Hansapank was most active on 26.4 million
kroons, was 1.55 kroons lower at 141.20.
* On the free market, Norma traded 2.2 million
kroons to close 1.8 kroons lower at 73.50 kroons.
(A complete report follows)
(See index on stock exchange web site:
http://www.tse.ee/online/total.htm)
Shares on the Estonian stock
exchange were mixed on Thursday as prices tried to move higher,
but fell back and dealers not optimistic for a recovery on
Friday ahead of the long weekend.
Total turnover on the main list was 59.7 million kroons and
the Talse index slipped 0.79 percent to 266.70.
"Prices tried to rise in the morning but fell back with some
investors profit taking in the afternoon," one dealer said.
With a long weekend of four days coming up, dealers did not
think the bourse would attempt to rally again.
"Tomorrow will not really help as people will be getting out
of the city early for the long weekend followed by a three day
week," another trader said.
Hansapank was the most active stock with 26.4 million kroons
traded to drop 1.55 kroons to close at 141.20 kroons.
Forekspank turned over of 11.1 million kroons and lost two
kroons to finish at 188.50 kroons.
Hoiupank announced after the bourse closed that it
was going to postpone its move to the Lithuanian market and
focus on the Russian and Ukrainian banking markets.
However, dealers did not believe that the change of plans
will affect the stock's price.
"It will make some investors reconsider their involvement
with the bank," one dealer said.
"But the bank's results from the local market are strong and
its price will not be affected by the news," he added.
The free market saw trade of 10.1 million kroons with
privatisation vouchers the most active with trade of 3.9 million
kroons to be 0.08 kroons higher on 0.288 kroons.
"The coming big privatisations like Hotel Olympia are what
usually promotes the interest in securities as part of the lots
will be sold to securities holders," one trader said.
Rakvere was traded down to end at 13.40 kroons,
0.65 kroons lower with 1.4 million kroons traded.
"It was the suspension news that took the stock lower, but
there were plently of buyers around 13.30, so I would not be
surprised if it regained what it lost today," one dealer said.
"The company is still good and it was the action of one
trader and his clients that caused the suspension," another
trader said.
Rakvere was suspended on Wednesday after the bourse
announced that an insider trading investigation had started into
trade of the company's stock on May 14 and 15.
-- David Mardiste, Tallinn newsroom, +372 620 9202,
reuters@reuters.ee
